lines: I did. Still breathing, still standing. That counts for more than it sounds.
Back to the village in one piece. I will remember who helped make that true.
I am here, breathing, and trying not to <shake>shake</shake>. That is enough for now.
The danger passed close, but it did not take me with it.
I made it through. My hands are still catching up to that fact.
I am alive, and right now that feels like a full day's work.
I heard the noise, felt the fear, and still found my way back.
My legs held, my breath held, and somehow so did I.
I would like a quieter day after that, if the world is taking requests.
Surviving does not feel heroic yet. Mostly it feels like breathing again.
I made it behind a door before my legs stopped shaking.
The healer says the bruise looks worse than it is.
I kept moving until someone told me the danger was gone.
My ears rang for a while after the fighting stopped.
I lost a tool, but I did not lose myself.
Someone found me near the path and helped me home.
I am alive because the person beside me refused to run.
The golem drew the danger away at the right moment.
I slept for nearly a day once I knew we were safe.
Standing here now feels like a victory, even if I am sore.
I found a really good hiding place, but I cannot tell you or it stops being good.
The bell is loud up close. I learned that by mistake.
Today I found a place where grown-ups forget to look down.
I saw a chicken walk like it had important business.
I found a puddle shaped almost like a potato.
I practiced sneaking, but my shoes kept telling on me.
I learned that if you look busy, grown-ups give you fewer chores.
There is a spot behind the fence where nobody checks first.
I found a stick that is probably important. I am keeping it safe.
Today I ran very fast and only almost fell down.
My best hiding place has enough room to breathe.
I never hide somewhere I cannot get out by myself.
The golem can see my shoes in one spot, so I stopped using it.
I keep a snack near my favorite hiding place.
The other kids know one place, but not the really good one.
I can hear the bell from where I hide.
Grown-ups always look behind doors first.
I found a spot where cats give away anyone coming near.
I only hide during games or when someone scary visits.
A hiding place is bad if spiders like it too.
<jump>Hi again!</jump>
Hi! I remember your face a little.
Hello again! I was practicing saying hello first.
Hi! I saw you before, I think.
<jump>Hello!</jump> I said it before you did.
Hi again! I am taller than last time, maybe.
Hello! I was not hiding. I was just standing somewhere secret.
Hi! Did you come back on purpose?
Hello again! I know this greeting now.
<jump>Hi!</jump> I was just about to do something important.
Hi again! I remembered your face.
You came back! What are we talking about today?
Hello! I saw you by the well earlier.
Hi! Did you bring another story?
It is you again. That is good.
Hello! I have been practicing saying hello normally.
You are back! I was wondering where you went.
Hi again. I know your name now.
Oh, hello! I was just about to go play.
Hi! You found me before I found you.
I can say hello from here.
Hello from this safe distance.
I can <wavy>wave</wavy> from here. That counts.
Hi. I am staying right here.
Hello. This spot feels far enough.
I heard you. I am not coming closer yet.
I can see you from here, so this is close enough.
Hello, but I am keeping my feet where they are.
I will wave. Talking closer is for braver people.
Hi. I am near the grown-ups, which is where I am staying.
I can hear you fine from over there.
Hello. You can stay on that side of the path.
We can talk across the path where I feel safe.
You can talk from there if you want.
Hi. I like this much space between us.
I will stay by the door while we talk.
Say what you wanted to say. I can hear you.
I am not hiding. I am just standing somewhere safe.
We can talk, but please do not move closer suddenly.
Hello from here. Here is a good place for me.
Ask a grown-up. They like sounding certain.
I know where the puddles are and which door creaks loudest.
I can answer if it is about hiding, running, or snacks.
I know some things, but not the boring ones.
If the question is hard, I can point at someone taller.
I know the bell is loud, doors are sneaky, and mud follows you inside.
I might know. Is it about games?
Grown-ups know answers. I know shortcuts.
I can tell you which corner of the square is best for not being noticed.
The bell means find a grown-up and get inside.
I know which door is closest from every part of the square.
Grown-ups check the latches when the sky gets dark.
The golem stands near the bell when trouble starts.
I practice getting home fast without running into anyone.
Some doors stick when it rains, and I know which ones.
The bell is louder inside a house than you would think.
We count the children after everyone comes indoors.
I do not open a door during danger just because someone knocks.
The safest house is the one with grown-ups already inside.
I know the difference between the dinner bell and the danger bell.
Once I ran all the way around the well and did not fall in. That is the whole story, but it was <jump>very exciting</jump>.
I had a <wavy>dream</wavy> I was tall enough to see over every fence.
I counted every door on this side of the square. Then I forgot the number and had to start over.
One time I found a beetle and followed it until it went somewhere too boring.
I tried to jump over a puddle, but the puddle was bigger than my plan.
I saw two chickens argue. I do not know who won, but one walked away proudly.
I hid behind a barrel for so long that I forgot I was hiding.
I made a tower of pebbles, and then the wind was rude to it.
One time I ran faster than my shadow. Only for a little bit.
I found the best stick in the village, but then someone said it was just a stick.
I dropped a pebble in the well and waited forever for the splash.
A frog sat beside the well like it owned the whole village.
I once tried to count the well stones and forgot where I started.
Someone tied a bucket badly, and we heard it fall all the way down.
I saw my face in the water and waved before I remembered it was me.
We played around the well until a grown-up used my full name.
A cat looked into the well and jumped back from its own reflection.
I found the roundest stone near the well and still have it.
The well makes whispers sound spooky if you lean close.
I can carry the empty bucket by myself, but not the full one.
Why did the bell ring? Because it had something <jump>important</jump> to say!
If I stand very still, chores cannot see me.
Why did the door close? Because the wind was bossy.
Why did the chicken cross the square? Because I was chasing it.
What do you call a muddy boot? Mine, usually.
Why did the fence stay still? Because it was very good at its job.
I told a joke to a sheep once. It said baa. I think that means funny.
Why did the puddle laugh? Because I stepped in it by accident.
What is faster than a grown-up calling chores? Me, going the other way.
Why did the bed look tired? Because everyone keeps sleeping on it.
What does the bell eat for lunch? Ring sandwiches!
Why was the bell tired? Everybody kept ringing it!
The bell told a joke, but it went over everyone's head.
I asked the bell to whisper. It said DONG very quietly.
Why did the bell stay home? It was feeling a little rung out!
The bell is bad at hiding because you can always hear it.
What is the bell's favorite game? Tag, because it likes being hit!
I told the bell to stop shouting, but it did not listen.
Why did the bell cross the square? Somebody carried it.
The bell never forgets a joke. It keeps ringing it up!
